The Scenic Byways dataset contains a derivative of KYTC road centerlines that reflect roadsides and viewsheds selected by the Kentucky Transportation Cabinet, Office of Local Programs for their scenic, natural, cultural, historical, archaeological, and/or recreational value. This selection encourages the preservation, restoration, protection, and enhancement of the roadway and associated right of way although it does not prohibit the Kentucky Transportation Cabinet from making transportation-related improvements as deemed appropriate by the Cabinet. This selection meets the American Association of State Highway and Transportation Officials (AASHTO) guidelines for highways and are state maintained as part of the state Primary Road System. For general information about the program please refer to this page: https://transportation.ky.gov/LocalPrograms/Pages/Scenic-Byways.aspxor the FHWA program page at either of these locations: https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/byways/or https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/hep/scenic_byways/us_code.cfm. For the law defining the purpose, funding, program definitions, selection criteria, etc., please refer to KRS 177.571-576.<\/p>

This feature layer illustrates where nationally designated scenic byway routes are located. In September 2026, FHWA updated the layer for all National Scenic Byways and All-American Roads to include the 49 designations to the America\u2019s Byways® collection that were approved in 2021. On January 19, 2021, the U.S. Department of Transportation approved 49 designations to the America's Byways collection, including 15 All-American Roads and 34 National Scenic Byways in 28 states. This increased the number of America's Byways® to 184 in 48 states. America's Byways is the umbrella term for the 184 distinct roads designated by the U.S. Secretary of Transportation, and the collection includes National Scenic Byways and All-American Roads. <\/p>

Please email scenicbyways@dot.gov<\/a> with any questions related to the National Scenic Byways Program<\/a>.

Linked view of MnDOT hosted web feature service for Travelers' Resource inventory of sites along the Great River Road in Minnesota. Linked data is filtered by field status and used to create an ArcGIS Online view feature layer of the data for use in the public <\/span>Plan Your Trip<\/a> web map application.<\/span> <\/p>

The Great River Road Plan Your Trip web application is intended to help plan your Mississippi River adventure along Minnesota\u2019s Great River Road National Scenic Byway, and help enrich travelers' byway experience while on the road. It provides information about the byway route, the Mississippi River Trail bicycle route, over 700 points of interest, Native American lands and historic sites, as well as multi-modal connection points including train stations, excursion boat landings and airports. The Plan Your Trip application also includes the alignments of and hot links to Minnesota\u2019s 20 other state and national scenic byways, each offering its own special sense of place. <\/span><\/div>

Esri ArcGIS Online (AGOL) Hosted Feature Layer which provides access to the MDOT SHA Scenic Byways data product.<\/span><\/a><\/p>

MDOT SHA Scenic Byways data consists of linear geometric features which represent the geographic extent of roadways that are officially designated as Scenic Byways throughout the State of Maryland.  Maryland\u2019s 18 designated byways encompass 2,487 miles of beautiful roads and offer a taste of Maryland\u2019s scenic beauty, history and culture. Take the roads less traveled - including byways featuring nationally significant themes: The Star-Spangled Banner, Harriet Tubman Underground Railroad, Religious Freedom, Chesapeake Country, Charles Street, Historic National Road, and the Catoctin Mountain National Scenic Byways. Maryland belongs to a longstanding network of national and state byways that include the most distinct and diverse roads of our nation. These corridors embody archaeological, cultural, historic, natural, recreational and scenic qualities that are worthy of preservation and promotion. Maryland\u2019s Scenic Byway program enhances community pride, as well as visitor appeal, by encouraging the responsible management and preservation of the State\u2019s most scenic, cultural and historic roads.
 <\/p>

MDOT SHA Scenic Byways data is owned & maintained by the MDOT SHA OPPE Regional Intermodal Planning Division (RIPD). This data is updated on an As-Needed / Irregular basis. <\/p>

MDOT SHA Scenic Byways data consists of linear geometric features which represent the geographic locations of roadways that are officially designated as Scenic Byways throughout the State of Maryland. Maryland\u2019s 18 designated byways encompass 2,487 miles of beautiful roads and offer a taste of Maryland\u2019s scenic beauty, history and culture. Take the roads less traveled - including byways featuring nationally significant themes: The Star-Spangled Banner, Harriet Tubman Underground Railroad, Religious Freedom, Chesapeake Country, Charles Street, Historic National Road, and the Catoctin Mountain National Scenic Byways. Maryland belongs to a longstanding network of national and state byways that include the most distinct and diverse roads of our nation. These corridors embody archaeological, cultural, historic, natural, recreational and scenic qualities that are worthy of preservation and promotion. Maryland\u2019s Scenic Byway program enhances community pride, as well as visitor appeal, by encouraging the responsible management and preservation of the State\u2019s most scenic, cultural and historic roads.<\/p>

MDOT SHA Scenic Byways data is owned and maintained by the Maryland Department of Transportation State Highway Administration (MDOT SHA) Office of Planning & Preliminary Engineering (OPPE) Regional Intermodal Planning Division (RIPD). This data is updated on an As-Needed basis. This data was last updated in September 2019.<\/p>
